old: Every piece receives a unique Electronic Product Code (EPC) via RFID, its own digital passport. The unit control ledger tracks each item's full history, when it was received, which display case it's in, when it was viewed by an associate, when it left for consignment, and when it was sold. RFID handhelds can count an entire case of 50 items in seconds without handling a single piece.
new: Every piece is serialized as its own unit, with or without RFID. With RFID, the piece carries an EPC; without it, it carries its own unit ID. The unit control ledger follows each piece through its life cycle: received, transferred, on layaway, sold and returned. With RFID, a handheld counts a display case without handling a piece.

note: jw faq2 (repairs: integrate, no competitor names)
old: Teamwork Commerce is not a jewelry-specific POS with deep repair ticketing or appraisal management. For independent jewelers with heavy repair workflows, dedicated platforms like WJewel or Jewel360 may be a better fit. Teamwork is built for multi-location jewelry chains and luxury brands that need enterprise infrastructure: RFID serialization, omnichannel fulfillment, global compliance, AI clienteling, and SOC 2 security, capabilities that jewelry-specific POS platforms don't offer.
new: Teamwork Commerce is not a repair or appraisal system, and it does not handle trade-ins. It integrates tightly with the systems that do. The associate takes the deposit in Teamwork Commerce, the repair goes to your repair system, and its status comes back so the customer can be told the piece is ready to collect.
